key_findings.title: Rise of Vision‑Transformer and hybrid CNN‑ViT backbones
key_findings.source: Deep Learning-based Depth Estimation Methods from Monocular Image and Videos: A Comprehensive Survey
key_findings.summary: Vision Transformers and CNN‑ViT hybrids are increasingly adopted because they capture long‑range dependencies and improve cross‑domain generalization, though they impose high memory and compute costs.

key_findings.title: Zero‑shot and cross‑domain generalization via massive semi‑supervised data
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation
key_findings.summary: Models such as ZoeDepth, UniDepth and Depth Anything train on tens of millions of self‑annotated images, achieving strong zero‑shot performance on both indoor and outdoor benchmarks.

key_findings.title: Domain adaptation remains a bottleneck
key_findings.source: Deep Learning-based Depth Estimation Methods from Monocular Image and Videos: A Comprehensive Survey
key_findings.summary: Fine‑tuning, style‑transfer GANs, and other adaptation techniques are essential for transferring models across day‑night, indoor‑outdoor, and synthetic‑real domains, yet gaps in texture and illumination persist.

key_findings.title: Loss of fine‑grained detail on thin, distant, or reflective objects
key_findings.source: Deep Learning-based Depth Estimation Methods from Monocular Image and Videos: A Comprehensive Survey
key_findings.summary: Both self‑supervised and supervised approaches struggle with thin structures, far‑away items, and materials with specular or transparent properties, leading to blurred or inaccurate depth edges.

key_findings.title: Trade‑off between patch‑based refinement / diffusion models and real‑time inference
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation
key_findings.summary: PatchFusion, PatchRefiner and diffusion‑based generators (Marigold, GeoWizard) recover high‑frequency details but scale poorly with image resolution, limiting deployment in latency‑sensitive applications.

synthesis: Between 2023 and 2025 monocular depth estimation has shifted toward metric‑scale predictions powered by large‑scale semi‑supervised training and transformer‑based backbones. Zero‑shot models such as ZoeDepth and Depth Anything demonstrate impressive cross‑domain performance, yet their gains are counterbalanced by the persistent need for domain adaptation techniques to bridge gaps in illumination, texture, and synthetic‑real disparities. Vision Transformers and hybrid CNN‑ViT architectures improve global context and generalization but introduce prohibitive computational overhead for embedded or real‑time settings. A recurring limitation across surveys is the degradation of depth quality for thin, distant, or reflective surfaces, a problem that patch‑based refinements and diffusion generators can mitigate at the expense of latency and memory. Consequently, the field faces a triad of challenges: achieving efficient, transformer‑enabled models, devising robust adaptation pipelines, and preserving fine‑grained detail without sacrificing speed. Addressing these gaps will be crucial for deploying monocular depth systems in autonomous navigation, AR/VR, and industrial inspection.
